Procedure: Replacing CO2 cylinders when the system is tested or when the automatic fire extinguishing system operates

sections_target.text: This document sets out the steps for replacing the CO2 cylinders when the system is tested or when the automatic fire extinguishing system of the gas unit operates.

The automatic CO2 gas fire extinguishing system consists of a number of cylinders containing carbon dioxide gas in its liquid state under a pressure of approximately 80 bar. The cylinders are arranged in groups according to the quantity of gas required for extinguishing, and each group is dedicated to extinguishing a fire in a specific area matching the volume of gas inside these cylinders. There are extinguishing gas nozzles and flame detectors distributed as shown in the following table:

Each of the flame and heat detectors has two independent lines, and for the fire system to operate a fire alarm signal must come from one of the fire detectors on the first line together with an alarm from one of the fire detectors on the second line. The weight-release solenoid then moves, the fire system operates, and at the same time the emergency trip signal goes from the limit switch to the various components of the unit so that they stop, and the slow-motion (turning gear) system operates. When the automatic fire extinguishing system operates, the cylinders are discharged, in which case they are replaced.

Mohamed Mohamed El-Lawandy, General Manager. It was reviewed by Chemist Ahmed El-Sayed Ibrahim and Eng. Mohamed Hussein Gomaa, Head of Quality Assurance and Quality Control Sector, East Delta Electricity Production Company.

rows: Place the cylinder on the cylinder holder at its installation position
Remove protective cover A and place it in a safe place until it is reused, taking care not to pull the safety pin of the cylinder valve
Connect suspension arms B to the cylinder head

Place the cylinder hoist C under the cylinder and raise the cylinder until suspension arms B can be fixed to the weighing device D carrying the cylinder, making sure that the cylinder is installed in the correct valve-opening direction, as the cylinder valve has a specific opening direction
Remove the plug from the cylinder valve opening and fit the high-pressure hose E to the cylinder valve, taking care to fit a Klingerit gasket to ensure a tight connection

Introduction
This document sets out the steps for replacing the CO2 cylinders when the system is tested or when the automatic fire extinguishing system of the gas unit operates.
The automatic CO2 gas fire extinguishing system consists of a number of cylinders containing carbon dioxide gas in its liquid state under a pressure of approximately 80 bar. The cylinders are arranged in groups according to the quantity of gas required for extinguishing, and each group is dedicated to extinguishing a fire in a specific area matching the volume of gas inside these cylinders. There are extinguishing gas nozzles and flame detectors distributed as shown in the following table:
Flame detector | Heat detector | Nozzles | Number of cylinders | 
1 | 4 | 4 | 3 | Right combustion chamber
1 | 4 | 4 | 3 | Left combustion chamber
1 | 4 | 8 | 7 | Oil tank
Each of the flame and heat detectors has two independent lines, and for the fire system to operate a fire alarm signal must come from one of the fire detectors on the first line together with an alarm from one of the fire detectors on the second line. The weight-release solenoid then moves, the fire system operates, and at the same time the emergency trip signal goes from the limit switch to the various components of the unit so that they stop, and the slow-motion (turning gear) system operates. When the automatic fire extinguishing system operates, the cylinders are discharged, in which case they are replaced.
